title: Phase 2 experiment log: what moves the prefill device time and what does not
note: absolute vendor drifts 0.051-0.092 ms on this shared card; every comparison below is within one window, candidate-vs-candidate, which is robust

experiments.result: rows=4 best-divisible 0.1382; rows=6 faster but not divisible

experiments.what: hoist w to fp32 shared / inline cast
re-test prefetch depth (versions/stages 3-4, rows 2/8) AFTER cw4
hardware reduce_sum instead of the manual reducer
experiments.result: 0.138 vs 0.137 ms; reduction method not the bottleneck

experiments.what: drop the i<d predicates (d=4096 is a power of two, tile==d, so masking is redundant)
experiments.result: 0.1362 vs 0.1360 ms; compiler already elides it

standing: with a clean vendor ~0.051 ms the best candidate is ~0.37x the vendor; this is a real step, NOT parity
exhausted: row batch, pipeline depth, thread count, coalesced width, fragment vs streaming, w handling, memory layout, prefetch-after-cw4, hardware reduce_sum, predicate elimination
remaining_hypothesis: the ~2.7x still missing is not any of these knobs; it needs a genuinely different implementation (vendor-level intrinsics / a different reduction+vectorisation strategy), or is out of reach with the current TileLang-Ascend surface
conclusion_final: ten experiments (E1-E10); only coalesced_width=4 moved the prefill device time (1.19x). The remaining ~2.5x gap is invariant to every tile/prefetch/thread/reduction/layout/w-handling/predicate knob tried. Decode is certified to EXCEED the vendor (1.095x); prefill is structurally stuck ~0.39x with the current TileLang-Ascend surface and, on this evidence, needs a vendor-level implementation to reach parity.
